```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_2022_crime.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Sort df by borough to have a consistent order
df = df.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build binary adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1.0

# Row-standardize weights
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
print('Row sums (should be neighbor counts):', row_sums[:10])
W = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Compute Moran's I
x = df['Crime_value'].values
z = x - x.mean()

# S0 = sum of all weights
S0 = W.sum()
print('S0:', S0)
print('n:', n)

numerator = np.sum(W * np.outer(z, z))
denominator = np.sum(z ** 2)
moran_I = (n / S0) * (numerator / denominator)

print('Observed Moran I:', moran_I)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_permutations = 1000
perm_stats = []

for _ in range(n_permutations):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.sum(W * np.outer(z_perm, z_perm))
    I_perm = (n / S0) * (num_perm / denominator)
    perm_stats.append(I_perm)

perm_stats = np.array(perm_stats)
p_value = np.mean(perm_stats >= moran_I)

print('Permutation test p-value (one-sided, >= observed):', p_value)
print('Mean of null distribution:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Std of null distribution:', perm_stats.std())
print('Min null:', perm_stats.min())
print('Max null:', perm_stats.max())

# Also compute two-sided p-value for completeness
p_two_sided = np.mean(np.abs(perm_stats - perm_stats.mean()) >= np.abs(moran_I - perm_stats.mean()))
print('Two-sided p-value:', p_two_sided)
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_2022_crime.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop NaN borough (City of London)
nan_borough = df[df['Crime_value'].isna()]['borough'].values[0]
df_clean = df.dropna().copy()
adj_clean = adj[(adj['borough'] != nan_borough) & (adj['neighbor'] != nan_borough)].copy()

df_clean = df_clean.sort_values('borough').reset_index(drop=True)
boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build binary adjacency matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1.0

# Row-standardize weights
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W = W / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Compute observed Moran's I
x = df_clean['Crime_value'].values
z = x - x.mean()
S0 = W.sum()
denominator = np.sum(z ** 2)
numerator = np.sum(W * np.outer(z, z))
moran_I = (n / S0) * (numerator / denominator)

print('Observed Moran I:', moran_I)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_permutations = 1000
perm_stats = []

for _ in range(n_permutations):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.sum(W * np.outer(z_perm, z_perm))
    I_perm = (n / S0) * (num_perm / denominator)
    perm_stats.append(I_perm)

perm_stats = np.array(perm_stats)
p_value = np.mean(perm_stats >= moran_I)

print('Permutation test p-value (one-sided, >= observed):', p_value)
print('Mean of null distribution:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Std of null distribution:', perm_stats.std())
print('Min null:', perm_stats.min())
print('Max null:', perm_stats.max())

# Two-sided p-value
p_two_sided = np.mean(np.abs(perm_stats - perm_stats.mean()) >= np.abs(moran_I - perm_stats.mean()))
print('Two-sided p-value:', p_two_sided)

# Count how many permutations exceeded observed
count_ge = np.sum(perm_stats >= moran_I)
print('Count >= observed:', count_ge, 'out of', n_permutations)
```
